transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Nolan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sam Cortez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, AtlasEdge), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Tess Huang (Product), Devon Park (SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on benchmarks, integration approach (OpenAI-compatible endpoints vs SDK), function/tool-calling needs for robot orchestration, and timeline for a two-week pilot sprint. Customer is latency-sensitive for teleops commands but wants cost predictability for fleet-scale inference.

Topics:
- Workload sizing: expected QPS, burst patterns, token lengths
- Integration options: SDKs (python/node), HTTP OpenAI-compat endpoints, function calling for structured commands
- Benchmarks: latency p50/p95, token cost, failure/fallback behavior, KV cache effectiveness
- Security: VPC/private deployment, KMS, audit logs
- Success criteria and timeline for a 2-week POC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared Nolan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. quick round, i'm Jared from Redwood, AE. Priya and Sam our SEs. go ahead and intro from atlasedge?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hi hi, lena here, CTO. we run the fleet control plane and the high level goal is to evaluate a hosted POC first but we might need a private/VPC for production.
[00:17] Marco Ruiz: Marco, lead ML eng, i'll be doing the benchmark runs and integration with our command router.
[00:20] Tess Huang: Tess, product, i'll own acceptance criteria.
[00:22] Devon Park: Devon, SRE, i'll be doing network and security checks.
[00:25] Priya Shah: awesome thanks. agenda - map out the POC scope: workload, endpoints (openai-compat vs SDK), tool-calling needs for structured robot commands, and a benchmark plan. sound good?
[00:33] Lena Ortiz: yes, and we want to make sure that commands issued to robots are strict JSON schema so we don't get malformed instructions out in the field.
[00:40] Priya Shah: totally. Redwood supports structured output via JSON schema and we can enforce model responses using function calling or structured output options. sometimes transcription shows "function calling" as function... but actual behavior is the same — you get validated, typed output.
[00:55] Marco Ruiz: on workload - our real-time teleops path is small payloads, usually 12-40 tokens per step, but we also have longer status summaries up to ~400 tokens. avg token length per request probably 80. traffic: baseline 40 QPS, bursts to 250 QPS during shift changes.
[01:14] Sam Cortez: ok thats helpful. are those user-facing latencies or backend comps?
[01:17] Marco Ruiz: user-facing, so p95 target ideally under 250ms for the teleops commands.
[01:22] Priya Shah: that's tight. for p95 <250ms we typically recommend a dedicated capacity pool or a hosted plan with pinned low-latency model variants. we can suggest batching knobs but batching hurts for single-token teleops so caching/prefix caching + model routing is more useful.
[01:38] Devon Park: we want to avoid any out-of-band training data retention; what does Redwood keep?
[01:43] Jared Nolan: by default hosted is multi-tenant and doesn't retain customer prompt contents for training, we can provide SOC2 docs and data retention policy. for Private or Dedicated you have more controls, and KMS integration for keys. we'll attach the security packet.
[01:57] Tess Huang: success criteria: functionally correct commands (>=98% parseable to our JSON schema), p95 latency <250ms for short commands, cost <= $X per 1000 tokens (we'll give numbers), and stability for 48-hour soak.
[02:10] Priya Shah: nice clear criteria. for the POC we suggest two benchmark profiles: 1) teleops (1-80 tokens, 40-250 QPS) focus on latency and error rate, 2) summary workloads (200-400 tokens, 5-10 QPS) focus on throughput and cost.
[02:26] Marco Ruiz: we'll provide a dataset: 2k teleops examples + 500 summary tasks.
[02:30] Jared Nolan: perfect. for integration options: we have SDKs in python/node and direct OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints. which do you prefer?
[02:38] Tess Huang: we prefer server-side integration in python for the command router but may do a lightweight edge/JS client for diagnostics.
[02:45] Priya Shah: great - we'll provide both SDK snippets and raw HTTP examples. note on OpenAI-compat: headers and payloads are mostly identical but we expose Redwood-specific routing params for model variants and compute tiers.
[02:58] Marco Ruiz: any differences for function-calling? we plan to use function-like calls to get typed command objects.
[03:03] Priya Shah: function-calling is supported; two approaches: 1) use OpenAI-compatible function call schema and Redwood will enforce return shape, 2) use Redwood structured-output which is a bit more opinionated but gives stronger validation and automatic KV cache hints. either approach works; we'll include samples for both.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: KV cash? sorry "KV cache" — i keep seeing "kv cash" in docs.
[03:24] Sam Cortez: yes that's a transcription quirk, it's KV cache — it stores computed prefixes and context to reduce token spend.
[03:30] Marco Ruiz: speaking of token spend, for the summaries we need a recommended quantized model — any guidance?
[03:35] Priya Shah: we can recommend a quantized variant that preserves quality for summarization. Redwood Optimize will suggest specific quantization and batching levels based on sample runs; part of the POC is to run the optimize job and see cost/quality tradeoffs.
[03:49] Devon Park: network: we will probably do hosted POC behind VPC peering, maybe dedicated later. we need egress IPs whitelisted. are static ips available for hosted?
[03:58] Jared Nolan: hosted can provide fixed egress IPs on request for pilot; for production dedicated or private will give you full control. we'll share the network checklist.
[04:06] Tess Huang: can we get tracing and per-request token breakdowns for debugging?
[04:10] Priya Shah: yes Redwood Console exposes per-request tokens, model name, latency, and trace IDs. we can also stream logs to your datadog or S3 if you want.
[04:18] Marco Ruiz: for benchmarks, what harness do you prefer? we typically use locust + custom scripts.
[04:22] Sam Cortez: we usually provide a lightweight harness (python + async) that hits the OpenAI-compat endpoints and collects p50/p95, errors, token counts. we'll include a locust example if you want.
[04:31] Marco Ruiz: good. how do rollbacks/fallbacks work if a model is overloaded?
[04:35] Priya Shah: Redwood has smart routing rules — you can set policies to fallback to a cheaper model or a local cached response on overload. for strict commands though you may prefer falling back to a queued retry rather than a different model to avoid format drift.
[04:49] Lena Ortiz: timeline? we want pilot data in two weeks. is that feasible?
[04:53] Jared Nolan: yes, we can do a two-week sprint: week 1 instrument + baseline hosted runs, week 2 optimize and a 48-hour soak. schedule a kickoff next week and we'll start prep now.
[05:02] Tess Huang: ok that matches our internal expectation. who will run the first benchmark?
[05:05] Marco Ruiz: i'll run with Priya's harness but we'll need sample keys and cleared network.
[05:10] Priya Shah: we'll provide an API key scoped to the POC, sample SDK snippets, and the harness. we'll also template the function-calling schemas for your robot commands.
[05:18] Devon Park: on encryption at rest — bring-your-own-key with KMS is mandatory for us in prod. is BYOK supported in Private?
[05:24] Jared Nolan: yes BYOK supported in Private and Dedicated models. hosted can integrate with cloud KMS for enterprise accounts; we'll include the KMS integration guide.
[05:34] Marco Ruiz: any gotchas with streaming responses and realtime controls? we prefer streaming for teleops to reduce perceived latency.
[05:40] Priya Shah: streaming is supported; be mindful of partial outputs and ensure your parser can handle chunked JSON. we usually recommend the function-calling path for strict schemas, and streaming of the final command only after it's validated client-side.
[05:55] Tess Huang: what about observability around hallucinations or malformed commands?
[05:59] Priya Shah: Redwood Console can alert on schema parse failures and trigger regression checks tied to a ground-truth prompt set. we'll show you the dashboards in the demo.
[06:09] Lena Ortiz: costs — can you give a ballpark?
[06:12] Jared Nolan: we'll send two scenarios: hosted baseline and dedicated reserved nodes with committed throughput. pricing will include token unit rates, reserved capacity monthly cost, and estimated POC spend.
[06:21] Marco Ruiz: perfect. to recap: priya will draft benchmark plan; jared sends pricing/security; we provide datasets and network details; schedule kickoff week of 7/20.
[06:30] Jared Nolan: yep, i'll follow up with calendar invite and links to the security pack, SDK snippets, and the POC checklist.
[06:36] Tess Huang: thanks all, feel good about this.
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: thanks.

End of transcript.
